html:
ChatGPT is a chatbot made by OpenAI of San Francisco and released to the public on 30 November 2022. It answers questions and writes and edits text and code in plain conversation, and it made large language models an everyday tool.

It runs on a GPT model, a generative pre-trained transformer: a neural network trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next word, then tuned with human feedback to follow instructions. The transformer design came from a 2017 paper by Google researchers. OpenAI had offered GPT-3 to developers since 2020, but the free chat window was what caught on. It reached about 100 million users in two months, then the fastest growth of any consumer app.

It set off the AI boom. Google, Meta, Anthropic and Chinese firms rushed out rivals, and the chipmaker Nvidia became one of the most valuable companies in the world. Schools, publishers and governments argued over cheating, copyright, jobs and safety. By early 2026 it had some 900 million weekly users. It stands in a line of shifts in computing that runs back through the smartphone to the World Wide Web.
